The frame: Triple Bottom Line

☕ TBL FRAME (1994)
Elkington (1994): a company should be judged on three results, not just one. Profit only counts as success if people and the planet are not paying for it.
People
Farmers get training and loans; partners get health cover, shares and tuition support.
Planet
Greener Stores, personal cups, plant-based milk, a LEED Platinum roasting plant.
Profit
“Ethical coffee” supports a premium brand: $37.2 bn revenue in FY2025.
Our question: does Starbucks do this because it is right, or because it sells more coffee? We think both, and TBL says that is fine, as long as the claims are true.

One cup, five theories

Follow the coffee from the farm to your hand. Every step is one theory from our course.

特调 SPECIAL · 咖啡 COFFEE · 茶饮 TEA
5 CORE COURSE THEORIES
1

Sustainable
Supply Chain

ON THE FARM

Manage every link, from raw material to customer, with social and environmental rules, not just the lowest price.

  • C.A.F.E. Practices (since 2004, made with Conservation International): third-party checks on labour, environment and pay on farms.
  • About 99% of its coffee is bought under these rules (FY2024).
  • Farmer Support Center in Pu'er, Yunnan (2012) trains local farmers for free.
Link: TBL “People” and “Planet” start here.
2

Sustainable
Production

ROASTING & STORES

Make the product with less energy, water and waste at every stage of operations.

  • Coffee Innovation Park, Kunshan (2023): US$220m roasting plant, LEED Platinum; rooftop solar gives about 20% of its energy.
  • Greener Stores (framework built with WWF and SCS Global Services): 10,000+ stores verified on energy, water and waste.
Link: helps “Planet”, and lower energy bills help “Profit”.
3

Sustainable
Marketing

AT THE COUNTER

Sell in a way that changes what customers do, and be honest about the real impact.

  • Bring your own cup: ¥4 off in mainland China stores.
  • Plant-based milk: no extra charge in the US since Nov 2024. Dairy is the biggest source of Starbucks' carbon emissions.
  • Risk: green claims must match reality (see “Where it falls short”).
Link: turns “Planet” goals into customer habits.
4

Sustainable Finance

THE MONEY BEHIND IT

Raise and use money for ESG goals. With a sustainability bond, investors know which projects their money pays for.

  • 2016: the first US corporate sustainability bond, US$500m, for ethical coffee buying, Farmer Support Centers and farmer loans.
  • Global Farmer Fund: US$100m in loans so farmers can replant and improve their farms.
Link: pays for the supply chain in ①.
5

Sustainable HRM

THE PEOPLE WHO RUN IT

Treat employees as long-term stakeholders: fair pay, health, training and wellbeing, so they stay and serve customers well.

  • Staff are called “partners”. Bean Stock gives eligible partners company shares.
  • Parent Care Program, China (2017): free critical illness insurance for parents of eligible full-time partners.
  • College Achievement Plan, US (2014, with Arizona State University): 100% tuition for a first bachelor's degree.
Link: TBL “People”; partners make ② and ③ work.
How they connect: ④ Finance → ① Supply chain → ② Production → ③ Marketing → Customer
⑤ HRM: partners at every step  ·  TBL: measures the result
☺

Where it falls short

☕ CRITICAL CASE REVIEW

“100% ethical”?

In 2024 the US National Consumers League sued Starbucks over this claim, citing labour abuses reported at some supplier farms in Brazil and Guatemala. A pass on paper is not the same as fair work on the farm.

Cups

Most drinks still leave in single-use cups. In China the ¥4 personal-cup discount is for counter orders; app and delivery orders still use throwaway cups.

Carbon

Most of its footprint is in the value chain (Scope 3): dairy, coffee farming, packaging. Starbucks does not control these directly, so the 2030 target is hard.

Workers

Since 2021, hundreds of US stores have voted to join a union, and partners went on strike in 2024. Good benefits alone do not build trust.

Our view

If we ran Starbucks China, we would:
→ allow personal or borrowed cups for app and delivery orders
→ publish farm audit results, not only the “99%”
→ make plant-based milk the easy choice (price and menu)
Verdict: a strong TBL example, but its best projects are the ones that also save money or build the brand. The real test comes in 2030.
Sources: Starbucks Global Impact Report (FY2024); Starbucks Form 10-K (FY2025); Starbucks Stories & News: “Starbucks issues first U.S. corporate sustainability bond” (2016), Global Farmer Fund, Greener Stores; Starbucks China newsroom: Parent Care Program (2017), China Coffee Innovation Park (2023); National Consumers League v. Starbucks (D.C. Superior Court, 2024); Elkington, J. (1994), “Towards the sustainable corporation”, California Management Review, 36(2).
